summary.text: Rick Allen is the Republican incumbent in Georgia's 12th District, which he has represented since 2015. A native of Augusta, he built a construction company over several decades before entering Congress, where he now chairs the House Committee on Education and Workforce. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

paragraphs.text: Allen was born in Augusta, Georgia, in 1951 and graduated from Evans High School in 1969.
He graduated from Auburn University in 1973 with a B.S. in building construction.

He worked as an estimator, project administrator, and assistant to the president at an Augusta construction firm before founding his own company, R. W. Allen & Associates, Inc., in 1976. His congressional biography says the company has operated in the Augusta and Athens communities for 50 years.

Allen received the Augusta Metro Chamber of Commerce Small Business Person of the Year award in 2008, took part in the first class of Leadership Augusta in 1980, and was inducted into the CSRA Business Hall of Fame in 2011, according to his House biography.
He ran for the Republican nomination for this seat in 2012 and lost the primary runoff to Lee Anderson.
He won the Republican primary on May 20, 2014, defeated Democratic incumbent John Barrow in the November 4, 2014 general election, and took office in 2015.
Allen served on the House Committee on Agriculture for eight years and sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee and the Education and Workforce Committee, according to his House biography.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), he serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Education and Workforce and as Vice Chair of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
According to his House biography, he and his wife, Robin, live in Augusta and have four children, and he is an active member of Trinity on the Hill Global Methodist Church.
